title: artemisia maritima subsp. gallica
intro: Artemisia maritima subsp. gallica, commonly known as European Sea Wormwood, is a subspecies of the annual or biennial herbaceous plant, characterized by its erect stems, narrow leaves, and small yellowish flowers. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiseptic properties, making it useful in treating various conditions such as wounds, digestive issues, and respiratory problems. The therapeutic actions of European Sea Wormwood include stimulating digestion, relieving flatulence, and alleviating symptoms of colds and flu. The bioactive constituents of this plant include sesquiterpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
